item: The re-index drain uses every core when the collector is idle, computes the next window while writing the current one, and commits by time held while collecting
refs: PR pending; R723; R724; user's re-index live-rate notes 2026-11-15
key_paths: src/api/backup_v2.py; src/analytics/store.py; src/analytics/reindex_parallel.py; src/backup/merge.py; tests/test_reindex_drain_settings.py; tests/test_reindex_pipeline.py; tests/test_reindex_throughput.py
summary: Three changes from the user's live measurements. (1) The serial precompute computes when/where/who (dates in the article's own language, R697) before index_article takes the write gate, as the pool did; it had been left to inline extraction under the gate, about 37% of each window. (2) R723: an idle collector gives the drain all_cores_worker_count() (OO_REINDEX_WORKERS still wins), and the next window's precompute starts in a helper thread before the current window is applied, only when it runs in the pool (a serial one would take the GIL from an apply holding the gate); windows are still applied in order, so the resume cursor is unchanged; OO_REINDEX_PIPELINE=0 turns it off. (3) R724: a running collector no longer means one article per commit: the import width bounded by a 2 s hold target (OO_REINDEX_COLLECTING_HOLD_TARGET_S, never above the general target, 0 = old rule), and a queued writer still ends a batch after 1 s. Published: workers_seen, hold_target_seen, precompute_wait_s, pipelined_windows. No speed-up figure is claimed until the user's next run measures it.
